Basic BottomSheet

 Use for presenting supplementary information, filters, or simple interactions. Keep content focused and provide clear ways to dismiss the sheet.

Action BottomSheet

 Perfect for task completion with forms on mobile layouts. Utilize the maxHeight property to ensure the sheet provides enough space without covering the entire screen.

When to Use BottomSheets

  • Providing supplementary content or contextual actions on mobile interfaces

  • Presenting filters, settings, or share menus without navigating to a new page

  • When the content is secondary but requires a dedicated view area

  • As a responsive alternative to dropdowns or large dialogs that would otherwise crowd the screen

Best Practices

  • Height Management: Avoid bottom sheets that span the full height of the screen. Use the maxHeight property to ensure users maintain context of the underlying page. The default is 80vh.

  • Content Density: Keep content concise and actionable. Avoid overwhelming users with dense text or overly complex forms in a bottom sheet.

  • Accessibility: Provide meaningful closeButtonAriaLabel values, especially when the default "Close" is not sufficiently descriptive for the context.

  • Focus and Dismissal: BottomSheet inherits focus management and backdrop/escape key dismissal from the underlying Dialog component, ensuring accessibility standards are maintained.
